meta.title: Routes
meta.description: The 36 route maps that adventure paths are built from: the ROGUE_ROUTE naming scheme, the six terrain types, each route's three-type wild Pokémon table, forest/cave item drop rarity bonuses, the calm/average/tough route sub-types, and the six FAIRY typing swaps EX makes. The route table itself is byte-identical between Vanilla and EX — all 36 routes (including Sinnoh's) exist in both versions.

prose.heading: The route naming scheme
prose.text: Every route is its own dedicated map with the name ROGUE_ROUTE_<Region>_<Type><N>. Hoenn routes carry no region prefix (ROGUE_ROUTE_FIELD0, ROGUE_ROUTE_CAVE0, ROGUE_ROUTE_MOUNTAIN1…), while Kanto, Johto and Sinnoh routes are prefixed (ROGUE_ROUTE_KANTO_FIELD0, ROGUE_ROUTE_JOHTO_CAVE0, ROGUE_ROUTE_SINNOH_201). Sinnoh routes use the region's real route numbers — 201, 205, 207, 209, 210, 212, 214, 215, 217 — plus three named locations: EternaForest, MtCoronet and IronIsland. The table is identical between the Vanilla and EX versions — all 36 routes, including Sinnoh's, exist in both; the only branch difference in the file is the wild type table of six routes (EX swaps one type to Fairy) and the legendary encounter table that lives in the same header.

prose.heading: Route types and wild Pokémon
prose.text: Each route carries a wild type table of exactly three types (for example, Hoenn Forest 0: Bug, Ghost, Poison), but the wild Pokémon on a route are not filtered by those three as a set: each route room picks a single hint type (cycling through the route's three), and only the very first wild encounter must match it — if no valid species has that type, the game falls back to any species — while the rest of the encounters roll unfiltered. Each route can also define an item drop rarity bonus, which is added to every item drop it makes — forests and caves are therefore the best routes for item hunting.

prose.heading: Calm, Average and Tough routes
prose.text: Every Route room on a generated path rolls a difficulty sub-type — calm, average or tough — and the sub-type tunes what the route offers, from encounter counts and trainer spawns to item drops and themed weather (matched to one of the route's three wild types). The roll itself shifts late in the run: from difficulty 9, the second Elite Four path, tough routes dominate.

roll.phase: Difficulty 9+ (from the second Elite Four path)

prose.heading: How routes appear on the adventure path
prose.text: A Route room is one of the 16 room types a generated adventure path can contain, alongside rest stops, team hideouts, honey trees, labs, shrines, signs and the final boss room. When a Route room is placed, the game picks a route from the full 36-route table with a seeded weighted roll: every route has a fixed delay seed (one of three), and for the current boss-difficulty tier only routes whose seed matches that tier are eligible — a pacing rule that brings different route groups into play as the ladder climbs (if none match, every route becomes eligible again as a fallback). Repetition is handled separately: an 18-slot history buffer remembers every route already placed on the current path, and those routes get zero weight, so the same route can never appear twice on one path. The room's warp then leads into the chosen route map. A route's region flag also sets its battle music: Kanto routes play Red/Green (Gen 1) tracks, Johto routes HeartGold/SoulSilver-style, Sinnoh routes Diamond/Pearl-style, and Hoenn routes keep the default Emerald themes.
